_readme: The CV skeleton: who Tom is, where he worked, when, and the structure of the page.
Taken verbatim from the 2026-08-05 base CVs (Tom_Norton_CV.docx and its Builder and
CS siblings), which is why the dates, locations and section shapes are exact.
The `bullets` here are the base CV's own text. They are the floor: what a role gets
when the bullet bank has nothing better, and part of what a tailored revision is
allowed to be made of. The bank is still the master library and its CANONICAL
version wins wherever the two disagree.
This copy is the seed. The live copy is cv-base.json in the private tom-bullet-bank
repo, and it wins whenever it exists: edit that one, not this one.
Shape. An entry is one employer or school: `left` and `right` are the bold header
line (name, then location on the right margin), and `roles` are the titles under it.
LexisNexis is one entry with two roles, because it is one employer. A project is not
an entry: it is a single bullet with a bold lead-in, which is how the base CV reads.
name: TOM NORTON
_contact_note: The phone number is deliberately NOT here. This repo is public and a phone number in
a public repo gets scraped; the same number on a CV sent to a named recruiter does
not. It lives in the bank's private copy of this file instead, and the poller says so
on the first build. Add it there as a second entry, after Barcelona:

Owned renewal risk forecasting for a $5.2M ARR enterprise book, giving CS and sales leadership a six-month view of at-risk revenue that shaped concession, escalation, and resourcing decisions; exceeded NRR targets three straight years (108-110%).

Used peer benchmark data to show an enterprise customer their reporting volume sat far below comparable companies, then built the case for an intake redesign that closed a $10K upgrade and moved annual case volume from dozens to hundreds.
Designed a QBR format pairing customer-specific product recommendations with usage data; tracked follow-through to drive adoption, later adopted across a 25-person CS team and by AEs.
Partnered with Product and Support to design and operationalize a three-stage review-comment-publish workflow that retained $70K ARR and became standard process for all new customers.
Built a post-implementation handoff playbook in Gainsight that standardized the onboarding-to-CSM transition; piloted it and rolled it out to all CSMs to flag adoption risk earlier.

Ran a defined renewal process across a $2M ARR corporate portfolio, opening fixed-term renewals three or more months ahead of expiry with a business review, running discovery for expansion opportunities, and closing proposals before the renewal date; converted qualifying auto-renewals into multi-year agreements.
Conducted quarterly business reviews mapping usage to time savings, surfacing roughly $150K in annual expansion opportunities.
Trained new hires on discovery calls and product demos, reducing ramp-up time 25% within one quarter.
Drove $1.2M ARR portfolio of law-firm customers, owning retention and satisfaction through strategic renewals, relationship development, and cross-sell of digital solutions.

factorial.text: Built the GTM funnel model for a $100M ARR HR-tech company evaluating market entry, working back from TAM to a 190-deal target, sizing a seven-person GTM team at $735K cost, and modeling CAC payback from 16 to 34 months across three scenarios. Only team selected to present to their VP of CX; scored 9/10.

debic.text: Designed the lead-scoring and routing logic and CRM data foundation behind a GTM strategy, the core initiative in a €1.5M demand-generation roadmap. Prototyped a redesigned lead-intake form and presented to Debic's Digital and Commercial leads.

gtm-health.text: Built a Python and Streamlit diagnostic for the RevOps analyst preparing a leadership briefing: models the bowtie funnel, flags anomalies in stage conversion, and reconstructs true deal stage history from HubSpot property-change logs, with a Claude-powered advisor layered on top.

handoff.text: Built a HubSpot and Zapier workflow that triggers structured onboarding the moment a deal closes, eliminating manual data entry and the dropped-context handoffs common between Sales and CS.
